senses.en: Causing strong dislike or a feeling of sickness.

ex.en: A disgustful smell rose from the forgotten food.
ex.zh: 被遗忘的食物散发出令人作呕的气味。

ex.en: The disgustful condition of neglected public toilets can discourage residents from using otherwise attractive parks.
ex.zh: 公共厕所因疏于维护而变得令人厌恶，可能使居民不愿前往原本很有吸引力的公园。

tip: 此词罕见且偏旧；现代英语通常用disgusting。
note: 真实但罕见、偏旧的词；通常用disgusting

senses.en: The jelly-like material inside a cell, outside the nucleus.

ex.en: Many chemical reactions take place in the cytoplasm.
ex.zh: 许多化学反应在细胞质中进行。

senses.en: A structure inside a cell with a specific job.

ex.en: The nucleus is the largest organelle.
ex.zh: 细胞核是最大的细胞器。

senses.en: A space in a cell filled with fluid.

ex.en: Plant cells have a large central vacuole.
ex.zh: 植物细胞有一个大的中央液泡。

senses.en: A network of fibers that gives a cell its shape.

ex.en: The cytoskeleton helps the cell move.
ex.zh: 细胞骨架帮助细胞运动。

senses.en: A single-celled organism without a nucleus, such as a bacterium.

ex.en: Prokaryotes were the first life on Earth.
ex.zh: 原核生物是地球上最早的生命。

senses.en: An organism whose cells have a nucleus.

ex.en: Plants, animals and fungi are eukaryotes.
ex.zh: 植物、动物和真菌都是真核生物。

senses.en: A coat made from waterproof material.

ex.en: She pulled on her mackintosh before walking into the rain.
ex.zh: 她穿上雨衣，然后走进雨中。

ex.en: A durable mackintosh can encourage people to walk rather than drive in wet weather.
ex.zh: 一件耐用的雨衣能鼓励人们在雨天步行而不是开车。

tip: 英式用词，略显老派；不指苹果电脑。

senses.en: Relating to cells without a nucleus.

ex.en: Prokaryotic cells are much smaller than ours.
ex.zh: 原核细胞比我们的细胞小得多。

senses.en: Relating to cells with a nucleus.

ex.en: Eukaryotic cells contain many organelles.
ex.zh: 真核细胞含有许多细胞器。

senses.en: Relating to very small living things such as bacteria.

ex.en: Microbial life thrives in the soil.
ex.zh: 土壤中微生物生命繁盛。

senses.en: A microorganism that causes disease.

ex.en: The pathogen spreads through contaminated water.
ex.zh: 这种病原体通过受污染的水传播。

senses.en: Able to cause disease.

ex.en: Most bacteria are not pathogenic.
ex.zh: 大多数细菌不致病。

senses.en: A substance that causes the body to produce antibodies.

ex.en: Vaccines expose the body to a harmless antigen.
ex.zh: 疫苗让身体接触无害的抗原。

senses.en: Giving someone a vaccine to protect against disease.

ex.en: Inoculation against smallpox began in the 1700s.
ex.zh: 天花接种始于18世纪。

senses.en: to provoke someone into acting through persistent pressure or annoyance
a pointed stick used to make animals move
something that strongly pushes a person to act

ex.en: His teasing goaded me into joining the race.
ex.zh: 他的取笑激得我参加了比赛。

ex.en: Competitive school environments may goad students into pursuing high grades at the expense of genuine understanding.
ex.zh: 竞争激烈的学校环境可能迫使学生追逐高分，而忽视真正理解知识。

col: goad someone into doing something｜激某人做某事
goad someone on｜不断刺激某人行动
a goad to action｜行动的驱动力
tip: 常用goad sb into doing，通常含负面刺激。

senses.en: A type of white blood cell that fights infection.

ex.en: Lymphocytes recognize invading germs.
ex.zh: 淋巴细胞能识别入侵的病菌。

senses.en: A white blood cell.

ex.en: Leukocytes increase during infection.
ex.zh: 感染时白细胞会增加。

senses.en: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.

ex.en: Hemoglobin gives blood its red color.
ex.zh: 血红蛋白使血液呈红色。

senses.en: A small blood cell that helps blood to clot.

ex.en: Platelets stop bleeding from small cuts.
ex.zh: 血小板能止住小伤口的出血。

senses.en: Relating to the movement of blood around the body.

ex.en: The heart is the center of the circulatory system.
ex.zh: 心脏是循环系统的中心。

senses.en: Relating to breathing.

ex.en: Smoking causes respiratory diseases.
ex.zh: 吸烟会引起呼吸系统疾病。

senses.en: the Western world, especially Europe and North America

ex.en: This old atlas describes the occident in great detail.
ex.zh: 这本旧地图集非常详细地描述了西方世界。

ex.en: Historical accounts often contrasted the occident with the orient, overlooking the considerable diversity within both regions.
ex.zh: 历史记述常把西方与东方对照，却忽视了两个地区各自内部的巨大差异。

col: the Orient and the Occident｜东方与西方
tip: 旧式用语，通常写作the Occident；现代多用the West。

senses.en: Relating to glands that release hormones into the blood.

ex.en: The thyroid is part of the endocrine system.
ex.zh: 甲状腺是内分泌系统的一部分。

senses.en: Relating to the skeleton; very thin.

ex.en: Skeletal muscles move the bones.
ex.zh: 骨骼肌带动骨骼运动。

senses.en: Relating to mammals.

ex.en: The mammalian heart has four chambers.
ex.zh: 哺乳动物的心脏有四个腔。

senses.en: An animal with a hard outer shell and jointed legs, such as an insect or crab.

ex.en: Arthropods make up most animal species.
ex.zh: 节肢动物占动物物种的大多数。

senses.en: A soft-bodied animal, often with a shell, such as a snail or octopus.

ex.en: Octopuses are clever mollusks.
ex.zh: 章鱼是聪明的软体动物。

senses.en: A complete change of form, such as a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.

ex.en: Frogs undergo metamorphosis from tadpoles.
ex.zh: 青蛙从蝌蚪经过变态发育而来。

senses.en: in accordance with a law, rule, or agreement

ex.en: Pursuant to our agreement, your deposit will be refunded.
ex.zh: 根据我们的协议，你的押金将予以退还。

ex.en: Pursuant to environmental regulations, factories must treat wastewater before releasing it into local rivers.
ex.zh: 根据环境法规，工厂必须先处理废水，才能将其排入当地河流。

col: pursuant to an agreement｜根据协议
tip: 几乎总用于pursuant to，常见于法律等正式文本。

senses.en: The hard case in which a caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

ex.en: The butterfly emerged from its chrysalis.
ex.zh: 蝴蝶从蛹中钻了出来。

senses.en: A silk covering that some insects make to protect themselves while changing form.

ex.en: Silkworms spin cocoons of fine thread.
ex.zh: 蚕吐出细丝结茧。

senses.en: A young insect that looks like a small adult; a spirit in myths.

ex.en: Dragonfly nymphs live underwater.
ex.zh: 蜻蜓的若虫生活在水下。

senses.en: Shedding old feathers, skin or shell to make way for new growth.

ex.en: Crabs are soft and vulnerable after molting.
ex.zh: 螃蟹蜕壳后身体柔软、容易受伤。

senses.en: A hard outer covering that supports and protects an animal's body.

ex.en: Insects have an exoskeleton made of chitin.
ex.zh: 昆虫有几丁质构成的外骨骼。

senses.en: A skeleton inside the body.

ex.en: Vertebrates have an endoskeleton of bone.
ex.zh: 脊椎动物有骨质内骨骼。

senses.en: To swell or become larger because of pressure from inside.

ex.en: Too much gas can distend your stomach after meals.
ex.zh: 饭后过多的气体会使你的胃胀大。

ex.en: During digestion, excess gas may distend the abdomen, causing discomfort that can affect daily activities.
ex.zh: 消化过程中，多余气体可能使腹部胀大，造成影响日常活动的不适。

col: distended with gas｜因气体而膨胀
tip: 多用于医学，强调内部压力导致胀大。

senses.en: A strong band of tissue that connects a muscle to a bone.

ex.en: She injured a tendon in her ankle.
ex.zh: 她脚踝的一条肌腱受了伤。

senses.en: A strong band of tissue that connects bones at a joint.

ex.en: The footballer tore a knee ligament.
ex.zh: 这名足球运动员膝盖韧带撕裂。

senses.en: A mammal whose young develop in a pouch, such as a kangaroo.

ex.en: Most marsupials live in Australia.
ex.zh: 大多数有袋动物生活在澳大利亚。

senses.en: Relating to mammals whose young develop inside the mother with a placenta.

ex.en: Humans are placental mammals.
ex.zh: 人类是有胎盘哺乳动物。

senses.en: An animal that eats both plants and meat.

ex.en: Bears are omnivores.
ex.zh: 熊是杂食动物。

senses.en: An animal's resemblance to another species or object for protection.

ex.en: Through mimicry, a harmless fly looks like a wasp.
ex.zh: 通过拟态，一种无害的苍蝇看起来像黄蜂。

senses.en: Numerous and varied
A pipe system distributing or collecting gas or liquid

ex.en: The benefits of growing your own vegetables are manifold.
ex.zh: 自己种蔬菜的好处是多方面的。

ex.en: The manifold challenges of urban growth require cooperation between local authorities, businesses, and residents.
ex.zh: 城市发展面临多方面的挑战，需要地方政府、企业和居民共同合作。

tip: 形容词用法较正式，常修饰benefits、problems等复数名词。

senses.en: Living on or in another organism and taking food from it.

ex.en: Parasitic worms can live in the gut.
ex.zh: 寄生虫可以生活在肠道中。

senses.en: The science of naming and classifying living things.

ex.en: Linnaeus founded modern taxonomy.
ex.zh: 林奈创立了现代分类学。

senses.en: A major group in the classification of living things, below kingdom.

ex.en: All vertebrates belong to the phylum Chordata.
ex.zh: 所有脊椎动物都属于脊索动物门。

senses.en: A group within a species that differs slightly, often by region.

ex.en: The Siberian tiger is a subspecies of tiger.
ex.zh: 东北虎是虎的一个亚种。

senses.en: The formation of new species during evolution.

ex.en: Isolation on islands can lead to speciation.
ex.zh: 岛屿上的隔离可能导致物种形成。

senses.en: The line of ancestors from which a person or species descends.

ex.en: The lineage of whales goes back to land animals.
ex.zh: 鲸的谱系可追溯到陆地动物。

senses.zh: 兴趣广泛的；兼收并蓄的
senses.en: Including or appreciating a wide variety of things.
Relating to the Christian church led by the Pope.
A member of the Christian church led by the Pope.

ex.en: Her catholic tastes include jazz, pottery, hiking, and opera.
ex.zh: 她的兴趣十分广泛，包括爵士乐、陶艺、徒步和歌剧。

ex.en: A catholic approach to reading exposes students to diverse perspectives across literature, science, and history.
ex.zh: 兼收并蓄的阅读方式能让学生接触文学、科学和历史领域的多元视角。

col: a practising Catholic｜践行信仰的天主教徒
tip: 小写指广泛包容；指天主教或其信徒须大写Catholic。

senses.en: Remaining as a small, useless trace of something once important.

ex.en: The human appendix may be a vestigial organ.
ex.zh: 人类的阑尾可能是退化器官。

senses.en: Having a similar structure because of a shared ancestor.

ex.en: A bat's wing and a human arm are homologous.
ex.zh: 蝙蝠的翅膀和人的手臂是同源器官。

senses.en: Becoming similar or coming together.

ex.en: Sharks and dolphins show convergent evolution.
ex.zh: 鲨鱼和海豚表现出趋同进化。

senses.en: Developing in different directions.

ex.en: Island birds took divergent paths.
ex.zh: 岛上的鸟类走上了不同的进化道路。

senses.en: The evolutionary history of a species or group.

ex.en: DNA has reshaped our view of bird phylogeny.
ex.zh: DNA改变了我们对鸟类系统发育的认识。

senses.en: Relating to the evolutionary relationships between organisms.

ex.en: A phylogenetic tree shows how species are related.
ex.zh: 系统发生树显示物种之间的关系。

senses.en: to understand something in the wrong way

ex.en: I misconceived her silence as a sign of agreement.
ex.zh: 我误把她的沉默理解为同意。

ex.en: Policymakers may misconceive local needs if they fail to consult residents before introducing changes.
ex.zh: 政策制定者若不在推行改革前征求居民意见，就可能误解当地需求。

col: misconceive someone's intentions｜误解某人的意图
tip: 较正式；日常表达“误解”更常用misunderstand。

senses.en: A method of classifying organisms by shared features from common ancestors.

ex.en: Cladistics groups birds with dinosaurs.
ex.zh: 分支系统学把鸟类和恐龙归为一类。

senses.en: Breathing; the process by which cells release energy from food.

ex.en: Cellular respiration releases carbon dioxide.
ex.zh: 细胞呼吸会释放二氧化碳。

senses.en: The loss of water vapor from plant leaves.

ex.en: Transpiration pulls water up from the roots.
ex.zh: 蒸腾作用把水分从根部拉上来。

senses.en: The process of a seed beginning to grow.

ex.en: Warmth and water trigger germination.
ex.zh: 温暖和水分促使种子发芽。

senses.en: An animal that carries pollen from one flower to another.

ex.en: Bees are the most important pollinators.
ex.zh: 蜜蜂是最重要的传粉者。

senses.en: The male part of a flower that produces pollen.

ex.en: Each stamen holds a pollen sac.
ex.zh: 每根雄蕊都有一个花粉囊。

senses.en: The female part of a flower.

ex.en: Pollen lands on the top of the pistil.
ex.zh: 花粉落在雌蕊的顶端。

senses.en: next to or touching each other

ex.en: The two farms are contiguous.
ex.zh: 这两个农场相邻。

ex.en: Wildlife corridors link contiguous patches of forest so animals can move safely between them.
ex.zh: 野生动物走廊把相邻的森林斑块连起来，让动物能在其间安全移动。

tip: the contiguous United States 指美国本土48州。

senses.en: The organ that produces eggs; in plants, the part that holds the seeds.

ex.en: The ovary of a flower develops into a fruit.
ex.zh: 花的子房会发育成果实。

senses.en: The network of thread-like parts of a fungus.

ex.en: Mycelium spreads underground for meters.
ex.zh: 菌丝体在地下蔓延数米。

senses.en: A plant-like organism made of a fungus and an alga living together.

ex.en: Lichens grow on bare rock.
ex.zh: 地衣生长在光秃秃的岩石上。

senses.en: A plant with feathery leaves that reproduces by spores.

ex.en: Ferns covered the forest floor.
ex.zh: 蕨类植物覆盖着林地。

senses.en: A plant whose seeds are not enclosed in a fruit, such as a pine.

ex.en: Conifers are the best-known gymnosperms.
ex.zh: 针叶树是最著名的裸子植物。

senses.en: A flowering plant whose seeds are enclosed in a fruit.

ex.en: Angiosperms spread rapidly in the Cretaceous.
ex.zh: 被子植物在白垩纪迅速扩张。

senses.en: To kill someone or something, especially violently.

ex.en: In the old tale, a knight slays a dragon.
ex.zh: 在那个古老的故事里，一名骑士杀死了一条龙。

ex.en: Traditional legends often celebrate heroes who slay monsters to protect their communities from danger.
ex.zh: 传统传说常常颂扬那些杀死怪物、保护社区免受危险的英雄。

tip: 过去式slew，过去分词slain；常见于文学或新闻。

senses.en: Describing trees with cones and needle-like leaves.

ex.en: Coniferous forests cover much of Canada.
ex.zh: 针叶林覆盖了加拿大的大部分地区。

senses.en: Living for two years, or happening every two years.

ex.en: Carrots are biennial plants.
ex.zh: 胡萝卜是二年生植物。

senses.en: Plant tissue that carries water up from the roots.

ex.en: Water moves through the xylem to the leaves.
ex.zh: 水通过木质部输送到叶子。

senses.en: Plant tissue that carries sugars from the leaves.

ex.en: Phloem carries food to the roots.
ex.zh: 韧皮部把养分输送到根部。

senses.en: Tiny openings on leaves that let gases in and out.

ex.en: Stomata close in dry weather to save water.
ex.zh: 天气干燥时气孔会关闭以保存水分。

senses.en: A thick underground stem that stores food, such as a potato.

ex.en: Potatoes are tubers, not roots.
ex.zh: 土豆是块茎，不是根。

senses.en: to give someone excessive care, comfort, and protection

ex.en: They cosset their elderly dog with blankets and treats.
ex.zh: 他们给年老的狗盖毯子、喂零食，把它照顾得无微不至。

ex.en: Parents who cosset their children may unintentionally limit opportunities for them to develop independence and cope with everyday challenges.
ex.zh: 过分呵护孩子的父母可能无意中限制孩子培养独立性及应对日常挑战的机会。

col: a cosseted upbringing｜备受呵护的成长经历
cosseted guests｜受到悉心照料的客人
tip: 及物动词，常暗示照顾过度；名词用法已罕见。

senses.en: An underground stem that grows sideways and sends up new shoots.

ex.en: Ginger grows from a rhizome.
ex.zh: 姜是从根茎长出来的。

senses.en: An organism that makes its own food, such as a green plant.

ex.en: Plants are autotrophs that use sunlight.
ex.zh: 植物是利用阳光的自养生物。

senses.en: An organism that gets food by eating other organisms.

ex.en: All animals are heterotrophs.
ex.zh: 所有动物都是异养生物。

senses.en: Making food using energy from chemical reactions instead of light.

ex.en: Deep-sea bacteria survive by chemosynthesis.
ex.zh: 深海细菌靠化能合成生存。

senses.en: An organism that breaks down dead plants and animals.

ex.en: Fungi are important decomposers in forests.
ex.zh: 真菌是森林中重要的分解者。

senses.en: Dead plant and animal material, or waste left after something breaks up.

ex.en: Worms feed on detritus in the soil.
ex.zh: 蚯蚓以土壤中的碎屑为食。

senses.en: Someone favouring individual freedom and minimal government control
Favouring individual freedom and minimal government control

ex.en: My neighbour is a libertarian who values personal choice.
ex.zh: 我的邻居是一位重视个人选择的自由意志主义者。

ex.en: A libertarian approach to economic policy generally favours reducing government intervention and expanding individual choice.
ex.zh: 自由意志主义的经济政策取向通常主张减少政府干预，扩大个人选择空间。

col: libertarian views｜自由意志主义观点
libertarian principles｜自由意志主义原则
a libertarian approach｜自由意志主义的做法
tip: 强调个人自由和有限政府，不等同于liberal。

senses.en: Light produced by living things.

ex.en: Many deep-sea fish use bioluminescence.
ex.zh: 许多深海鱼会生物发光。

senses.en: Finding objects by sending out sounds and listening for echoes.

ex.en: Bats hunt insects using echolocation.
ex.zh: 蝙蝠利用回声定位捕捉昆虫。

senses.en: A deep sleep in which some animals spend the winter.

ex.en: Bears lose weight during hibernation.
ex.zh: 熊在冬眠期间体重下降。

senses.en: A period of inactivity in which growth stops.

ex.en: Seeds may stay in dormancy for years.
ex.zh: 种子可能休眠多年。

senses.en: Active during the day.

ex.en: Most songbirds are diurnal.
ex.zh: 大多数鸣禽是昼行性的。

senses.en: Behavior by which animals attract a mate.

ex.en: Peacocks display their tails during courtship.
ex.zh: 孔雀在求偶时开屏。

senses.en: infected with harmful bacteria, or relating to such infection

ex.en: The nurse cleaned the septic wound and changed its dressing.
ex.zh: 护士清洁了感染的伤口，并更换了敷料。

ex.en: Prompt treatment of bacterial infections can reduce the risk of septic shock and improve patient outcomes.
ex.zh: 及时治疗细菌感染可以降低脓毒性休克的风险，改善患者的治疗结果。

tip: septic tank 指化粪池；septic 不作“腐烂物”名词。

senses.en: Searching for food.

ex.en: Bees spend the day foraging for nectar.
ex.zh: 蜜蜂整天采集花蜜。

senses.en: Living in groups with division of labor and only some members breeding.

ex.en: Ants and honeybees are eusocial insects.
ex.zh: 蚂蚁和蜜蜂是真社会性昆虫。

senses.en: A chemical released by an animal that affects others of its species.

ex.en: Ants follow pheromone trails to food.
ex.zh: 蚂蚁沿着信息素踪迹找到食物。

senses.en: The release of eggs by fish or amphibians.

ex.en: Salmon return upstream for spawning.
ex.zh: 鲑鱼洄游到上游产卵。

senses.en: The period during which a baby develops inside its mother.

ex.en: Elephants have a gestation of about 22 months.
ex.zh: 大象的妊娠期约为22个月。

senses.en: A young animal that has just come out of its egg.

ex.en: Turtle hatchlings race to the sea.
ex.zh: 刚孵出的小海龟奔向大海。
